easy.def: To make a long, low sound because you are sad or in pain.
examples: The wind moaned.
He moaned in pain.
The ghost moaned.

more.def: To make a long, low sound, as when you are in pain or unhappy.
examples: The wind moaned in the chimney.
He moaned when he hurt his knee.
The old floor moaned under my feet.

easy.def: A large, wild crowd.
examples: A mob of people ran.
The mob was loud.
The crowd turned into a mob.

more.def: A large crowd of people that is noisy and hard to control.
examples: A mob of fans rushed toward the singer.
The angry mob shouted outside the building.
Shoppers formed a mob at the door of the store.

easy.def: Able to move.
examples: The mobile home has wheels.
The mobile library came.
The ship is mobile.

more.def: Able to move or be moved from place to place.
examples: The mobile library visited our town.
A mobile phone can be carried anywhere.
The stage is mobile and rolls to the gym.

easy.def: A hanging toy that moves in the air.
examples: The baby looked at the mobile.
The mobile has stars.
A mobile hangs over the crib.

more.def: A hanging toy or decoration whose parts move in the air.
examples: A colorful mobile hung over the crib.
The mobile spun in the breeze.
We made a mobile with paper birds.

easy.def: To make fun of someone.
examples: Do not mock others.
He mocked her accent.
They mocked the singer.

more.def: To make fun of someone by copying them in an unkind way.
examples: It is unkind to mock others.
He mocked her accent, and she felt sad.
The parrot mocked the cat's meow.

easy.def: Not real, for practice.
examples: We had a mock test.
The mock fire drill was today.
The mock trial was fun.

more.def: Done as practice or in imitation, not real.
examples: We took a mock test before the real one.
The class held a mock election.
The firefighters ran a mock rescue.

easy.def: A small copy of something.
examples: I built a model of a ship.
The model car is small.
He made a model airplane.

more.def: A small copy of a real thing, often to show how it looks or works.
examples: The model house had a tiny door.
The class made a model of the solar system.
He glued a model airplane together.

easy.def: A person who shows clothes.
examples: The model wore a dress.
Models walk on the stage.
She is a model.

more.def: A person whose job is to wear clothes to show them to others.
examples: The model wore a bright red coat.
Models walked down the long stage.
She worked as a model for a clothing store.

easy.def: Of the present time.
examples: We live in a modern house.
Modern cars are fast.
The modern world is busy.

more.def: Of the present or recent time, not of long ago.
examples: Modern phones can take pictures.
The new school is a modern building.
Modern doctors have many new tools.

easy.def: A little bit wet.
examples: The soil is moist after the rain.
The cake is moist and soft.
A frog has moist skin.

more.def: Slightly wet; damp.
examples: Keep the seeds in moist soil until they sprout.
The dog's nose was cool and moist.
Moist air from the ocean brought fog.

easy.def: A small animal that digs tunnels.
examples: The mole dug a tunnel.
A mole lives underground.
The mole has tiny eyes.

more.def: A small furry animal with tiny eyes and big front paws that lives underground.
examples: A mole dug a tunnel under the lawn.
Moles have tiny eyes and big paws.
The mole pushed up a pile of dirt.

easy.def: A small dark spot on the skin.
examples: I have a mole on my arm.
The mole is small.
She has a mole.

more.def: A small, dark, raised spot on the skin.
examples: I have a small mole on my arm.
The mole is brown and round.
He has a mole on his cheek.

easy.def: A word for your mother.
examples: My mom makes soup.
Mom hugged me.
I help my mom.

more.def: A word used for a mother, in everyday talk.
examples: My mom drives me to soccer practice on Tuesdays.
Her mom is a teacher at the high school.
Mom, may I have a snack?

easy.def: A very short time.
examples: Wait a moment.
It took a moment.
Just one moment!

more.def: A very short period of time, or a particular point in time.
examples: Wait a moment while I find my shoes.
At that moment, the lights went out.
The best moment of the trip was seeing the whale.

easy.def: A name for your mother.
examples: Mommy read me a story.
I love my mommy.
Mommy made lunch.

more.def: A word that young children use for their mother.
examples: The little girl ran to her mommy.
Mommy tucked me into bed.
My mommy drives a blue van.

easy.def: The day after Sunday.
examples: We have art on Monday.
See you on Monday!
Monday is when school starts again.

more.def: The day of the week that comes after Sunday and before Tuesday.
examples: On Monday, our class is going on a trip to the farm.
The library is closed on Monday.
Many people go back to work on Monday morning.

easy.def: Coins and paper you use to pay for things.
examples: I have money for a toy.
She saved her money.
Dad has no more money.

more.def: Coins and paper bills that people use to buy things or to pay for work.
examples: He saved his money for months to buy a new bike.
The class raised money for the animal shelter.
People use money to pay for food, clothes, and homes.

easy.def: A screen that shows pictures from a computer.
examples: The monitor is on the desk.
She looked at the monitor.
The monitor is bright.

more.def: The screen of a computer, which shows words and pictures.
examples: The computer monitor showed my game.
Dad bought a bigger monitor for his office.
The monitor went dark when the power went out.

easy.def: A student who helps the teacher.
examples: I am a hall monitor.
The monitor passed out papers.
The lunch monitor helped us.

more.def: A student or other person who has the job of watching over something.
examples: The hall monitor reminded us to walk.
The class monitor took the plates to the cafeteria.
A lunch monitor helped the little kids.

easy.def: To watch something over time.
examples: The nurse monitors my temperature.
The class monitored the plant's growth.
We monitor the weather.

more.def: To watch and check something over time.
examples: Scientists monitor the weather every day.
The nurse monitored the patient's heartbeat.
Our class monitored the growth of the bean plant.

easy.def: A man who lives and prays with other men.
examples: The monk prayed.
A monk lives at the temple.
The monk wore a robe.

more.def: A man who belongs to a religious community and lives a simple life of prayer.
examples: The monk lived in a quiet hall in the mountains.
A monk rang the temple bell.
The monks grew their own vegetables.

easy.def: An animal with long arms and a tail that climbs.
examples: The monkey climbed the tree.
A monkey ate a banana.
Monkeys swing from branches.

more.def: A furry animal with long arms and a tail that climbs trees.
examples: The monkey swung from branch to branch.
Monkeys live in warm forests.
A monkey peeled a banana at the zoo.

easy.def: A scary make-believe creature.
examples: The monster in the book was funny.
He drew a monster.
The monster had three eyes.

more.def: A large, scary creature in stories.
examples: The monster in the story turned out to be friendly.
She drew a purple monster with three eyes.
The children dressed as monsters for the party.

easy.def: About four weeks of time.
examples: A year has twelve months.
It is a new month.
I turn six next month.

more.def: One of the twelve parts of a year, such as May or June.
examples: June is the first month of summer.
My grandparents visit once a month.
It rained almost every day this month.

easy.def: The way you feel at a time.
examples: I am in a good mood.
Dad is in a happy mood.
She was in a bad mood.

more.def: The way a person feels at a certain time.
examples: I'm in a cheerful mood today.
Dad was in a good mood after the game.
The rainy day put her in a quiet mood.

easy.def: The big round light in the night sky.
examples: The moon is bright.
I see the moon.
The moon goes around the Earth.

more.def: The large ball of rock that travels around the Earth and shines at night.
examples: The full moon lit up the whole yard.
Astronauts have walked on the moon.
The moon takes about a month to go around the Earth.

easy.def: A smaller body that circles a planet.
examples: Jupiter has many moons.
Mars has two moons.
A moon goes around a planet.

more.def: A natural body that travels around a planet.
examples: Jupiter has dozens of moons.
Mars has two small moons.
Scientists study the moons of Saturn.

easy.def: The light from the moon.
examples: We walked in the moonlight.
The moonlight is soft.
Moonlight shone on the lake.

more.def: The light that shines from the moon at night.
examples: We walked home in the moonlight.
Moonlight shone on the quiet lake.
The room glowed with silver moonlight.

easy.def: The lesson that a story teaches.
examples: The moral of the story is to be kind.
What is the moral?
The moral is to work hard.

more.def: The lesson about right and wrong that you learn from a story.
examples: The moral of the fable is that slow and steady wins.
The fable's moral was to work together.
Can you tell me the moral of the tale?

easy.def: Having to do with right and wrong.
examples: It is a moral choice.
Telling the truth is a moral act.
A moral person tells the truth.

more.def: Having to do with what is right and wrong, or being good and fair.
examples: Telling the truth is the moral thing to do.
She made a moral choice to return the money.
A moral person treats others with respect.

easy.def: A larger amount.
examples: I want more milk.
She has more toys.
Can I have more?

more.def: A greater number or amount of something, or an extra amount.
examples: There are more stars in the sky than anyone can count.
Add a little more water to the paint.
We need two more players to start the game.

easy.def: The first part of the day.
examples: I wake up in the morning.
Good morning!
Birds sing in the morning.

more.def: The early part of the day, from sunrise until noon.
examples: The farmer feeds the chickens first thing in the morning.
Dew shone on the grass in the bright morning sun.
We have math class on Monday morning.

easy.def: Not able to live forever.
examples: People are mortal.
All living things are mortal.
The hero was mortal.

more.def: Having to die one day, as all living things do.
examples: All people are mortal.
The gods in the story lived forever, but humans were mortal.
The hero was mortal and grew old.

easy.def: A place to sleep for a night when you travel by car.
examples: We stayed at a motel.
The motel has a pool.
The motel is by the road.

more.def: A hotel by the road where people who travel by car can stay and park.
examples: We stopped at a motel for the night.
The motel had a pool and a parking lot.
The family stayed at a small motel on the way to the beach.

easy.def: A woman who has a child.
examples: My mother is kind.
Her mother is a nurse.
I help my mother.

more.def: A woman who has a child, or a female parent.
examples: My mother reads to me before bed.
The mother duck led her ducklings across the road.
He made a card for his mother on her birthday.

easy.def: Moving from one place to another.
examples: The wheel is in motion.
The motion of the waves is calm.
The car was in motion.

more.def: The act or state of moving.
examples: The gentle rocking motion put the baby to sleep.
The gentle motion of the boat made me sleepy.
Scientists study the motion of the planets.

easy.def: A machine that makes things move.
examples: The boat has a motor.
The toy has a small motor.
The motor is loud.

more.def: A machine that uses power to make something move.
examples: The boat has a motor that pushes it across the lake.
The toy car has a small motor.
The motor hummed when I turned on the fan.

easy.def: A two-wheeled vehicle with an engine.
examples: The motorcycle is loud.
He rides a motorcycle.
The motorcycle has two wheels.

more.def: A two-wheeled vehicle with an engine that you sit on and steer with handlebars.
examples: He rode a motorcycle down the highway.
The motorcycle roared past us.
A rider must wear a helmet on a motorcycle.

easy.def: To climb up onto something.
examples: He mounted the horse.
I mounted the stairs.
She mounted the bike.

more.def: To get up on something, such as a horse or a bike.
examples: The rider mounted the horse.
She mounted the steps to the stage.
He mounted the bike and rode away.

easy.def: A mountain.
examples: Mount Everest is tall.
We saw Mount Rainier.
The mount is snowy.

more.def: A word for a mountain, often used before a name.
examples: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth.
The climbers hiked up Mount Washington.
Mount Rushmore has four faces carved in stone.

easy.def: A very tall hill.
examples: There is snow on top of the mountain.
We drove up the mountain.
A goat lives on the mountain.

more.def: A very high area of land, much taller than a hill.
examples: It took the climbers three days to reach the top of the mountain.
The mountain was hidden in clouds.
A cold stream runs down the side of the mountain.

easy.def: A small animal with a long tail.
examples: A mouse ran under the bed.
The cat chased the mouse.
The mouse ate the cheese.

more.def: A small furry animal with a pointed nose, small ears and a long thin tail.
examples: A tiny mouse nibbled on seeds in the barn.
Mice can squeeze through very small holes.
The owl swooped down to catch a mouse.

easy.def: A small tool you move with your hand to use a computer.
examples: Click the mouse.
I move the mouse.
The mouse is by the computer.

more.def: A small device that you move by hand to point and click on a computer screen.
examples: I clicked the mouse to open the game.
He moved the mouse to the button on the screen.
A wireless mouse has no cord.

easy.def: The hair that grows above a man's lip.
examples: Grandpa has a moustache.
The man has a big moustache.
The moustache is gray.

more.def: The strip of hair that some men grow between their nose and mouth.
examples: Grandpa has a bushy gray moustache.
The actor wore a fake moustache.
He trimmed his moustache with scissors.

easy.def: The part of your face you eat with.
examples: Open your mouth.
The baby put the toy in her mouth.
My mouth is full.

more.def: The opening in the face that is used for eating and speaking.
examples: Open your mouth wide and say ahh.
The hippo opened its huge mouth.
She covered her mouth when she yawned.

easy.def: The place where a river ends.
examples: The ship sailed to the mouth of the river.
A town sits at the mouth of the river.
Birds gather at the river's mouth.

more.def: The place where a river flows into the sea or a lake.
examples: A city grew at the mouth of the river.
Many fish live at the mouth of the river.
We walked to the mouth of the stream.

easy.def: To go from one place to another.
examples: Do not move.
The snail moves slowly.
She moved her chair.

more.def: To change position or place, or to make something change its position.
examples: The clouds move across the sky in the wind.
Please move your bag so I can sit down.
The dancers moved in time with the music.

easy.def: To go live in a new home.
examples: We move next week.
They moved to a new town.
She moved away.

more.def: To leave your home and go to live in a new place.
examples: My family moved to a new town last summer.
They are moving to a bigger house near the park.
Our neighbors moved away, and new ones came.

easy.def: Moving from one place to another.
examples: I saw movement in the grass.
The movement of the clock hands is slow.
Dancers use graceful movements.

more.def: The act of moving, or a way in which a person or thing moves.
examples: We saw some movement in the bushes.
The dancer's movements were smooth and graceful.
The movement of the planets is very slow.

easy.def: A group of people working together for a cause.
examples: The movement helped clean the river.
They joined the movement.
A big movement for kindness.

more.def: A group of people who work together to change something.
examples: The movement for clean air began many years ago.
Many people joined the movement to protect the forests.
The students started a movement to recycle more.

easy.def: A story you watch on a screen.
examples: We watched a movie.
The movie was funny.
I like movies about animals.

more.def: A story told with moving pictures and sound, shown in a theater or on a screen.
examples: We saw a movie about dinosaurs at the theater.
The movie was long, so we took a break to eat popcorn.
Many movies are made from favorite books.
